# Two CAD expense lines on one USD bill, one of them on an account held to
# thousandths.
#
# The fuel line carries 1.819 CAD for 1.30 USD and the parts line 5.00 for
# 3.57. Their ratios differ in the third decimal because each was rounded to
# its own unit — a rate of 1.3992 produces both exactly — which is why the
# tool pools them rather than judging them against each other: 6.819 CAD over
# 4.87 USD is the cost of the USD this bill brought in, whichever order the
# splits are read in.
#
# What this fixture produces: one cost basis, and figures printed at the unit
# each split is held to. Shown at the cent the fuel line reads 1.82, which is
# not what the ledger holds, and nothing tells a reader that account apart
# from an ordinary CAD one.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_verify_costs.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Fuel
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	commodity_scu: 1000
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Parts
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD
	type: Accounts Payable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-01-10 * "A US bill whose two CAD lines were converted differently"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Expenses:Fuel 1.819 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		value: "1.30"
	Expenses:Parts 5.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		value: "3.57"
	Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD -4.87 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		value: "-4.87"
